definitions.definition: Professional application of knowledge, skills and competencies to generate a new business idea and launch an enterprise, pursuing growth while creating wealth, employment and social good.
Agent who buys factors of production at certain prices and combines them into a product to sell at uncertain prices in future.
Business organisation formed to provide goods and services, create jobs and contribute to national income, exports and overall economic development.
Blissful state of balance in which a person is fully immersed in a task and completely free from distracting thoughts.
Act of carefully examining the finance, skills, people and other resources one has or requires in order to start off well.
First principle of effectuation, stating that an entrepreneur starts with what is already in hand after taking stock of available means.
Entrepreneurial style adopted by those who are ambitious about creating a social impact and addressing social issues.
Iterative process of understanding the user, challenging assumptions and redefining problems to find alternative strategies and solutions that are not instantly apparent.
Activity of dividing a broad consumer or business market into sub-groups of consumers based on shared characteristics.
Group of consumers or organisations most likely to buy a company's products or services, on which marketing efforts are focused.
Subset of the market on which a specific product is focused, defining the features, price range and demographics it targets.
Situation in which customers look for more innovative products and services, so a company must develop to satisfy their needs.
Conceptual structure that supports the viability of a product or company and explains how it operates, makes money and achieves its goals.
Way of thinking about the startup process that stresses the business model over the plan and encourages customer discovery, development and iteration.
Exercise that identifies all the actions that take a product or service through a process.
One-page strategic management tool that defines and communicates a business idea by working through the fundamental elements of a business or product.
Exchange of value between a business and its customers, around which external and internal factors meet.
Product with just enough features to satisfy early customers and provide feedback for future product development.
Being in a good market with a product that can satisfy that market.
System of manufacturers or businesses sharing the common objective of producing a particular kind of goods or services.
Lateral thinking technique for solving any given problem innovatively, used here to study innovations in an industry.
Income that a business generates by means of its sales.
A distinct source of business income, such as one of the different services a business offers.
Costs incurred before starting a business, such as the vehicle, freezer, licence and signage of a food truck.
Costs incurred regularly irrespective of production and sales, usually calculated monthly, such as salary, rent and interest.
Costs that depend on the number of units produced and sold, such as raw material and packaging.
Point at which costs or expenses and revenues are equal, leaving no net loss or gain.
High-net-worth individual who provides financial backing to small startups, typically in exchange for ownership equity in the company.
Manner and approach of providing direction, implementing plans and motivating people.
Style that broadly distributes leadership responsibility so that people within a team and organisation lead each other.
Group technique for finding alternatives that can be used at all stages of the problem-solving process.
Principle of generating seemingly crazy or exaggerated ideas and not censoring them.
Temporary endeavour undertaken to create a unique product or service.
Detailed methodology for the systematic initiation, tracking and closing of a project.
Process of defining the scope, objectives and steps needed to get the work done, producing a project plan.
Smaller, manageable deliverables and groups of related tasks obtained by breaking down the scope of a project.
Act of designing a company's offering and image so that it occupies a distinctive place in the target market's mind.
Process of creating a new or modified position for a brand, company or product.
Way of increasing the distance between you and your competition by widening the value gap known as differentiation.
Name, symbol, mark, logo, word or sentence, or a combination, that companies use to distinguish their product from others.
Process of giving meaning to an organisation, product or service by creating and shaping an identity in consumers' minds.
Marketing a group of related products under a single master brand.
Strategy in which a company sells multiple brands in the same market to appeal to different customer segments.
Means adopted by a company to communicate with its customers or deliver products or services to them.
Gaining new consumers by persuading them to purchase a company's products or services.
Skills salesmen need to build relationships with customers, persuade them to make purchases and generate repeat business.
Strategy that sets out sales targets and tactics for a business and the steps to meet those targets.
Federal, state and local rules that startups must follow, balancing the interests of business with those of the public.
Arrangement in which two or more individuals share the profits and liabilities of a business venture.
